ads.title: Complete Lie
ads.url_found_via: AdImpact creative page (title, sponsor, first-air date 10/08/26, tone 'Negative'): https://host2.adimpact.com/admo/viewer/0efde999-3b84-49e2-b260-2b7c9e240d43. ads.transcript: Seen these ads? They're a complete lie. Records show not only is this woman actually from Texas. She didn't have any surgery as a minor, … But Jon Husted? He protected men who abused young girls by voting in the Senate to block the release of the Epstein files. … Maybe that's because Husted took over $116,000 from associates of Jeffrey Epstein—10 times more than any other senator. … Jon Husted should be ashamed.
ads.tone_reported: response/attack: rebuts an SLF ad, then attacks Husted (AdImpact classifies it as negative; Metro Weekly: 'Rebuts Anti-Trans Ad, Hits Husted on Epstein')
central_claims: The woman in the SLF ads is from Texas and did not have surgery as a minor
Husted voted in the Senate to block the release of the Epstein files
Husted took over $116,000 from associates of Jeffrey Epstein, 10 times more than any other senator

fact_checks.claim: The woman in the SLF ad is 'actually from Texas' and 'didn't have any surgery as a minor'
fact_checks.rating: No formal rating; consistent with News 5 Cleveland reporting that records show she lived and was treated in Texas and had the surgery at 19, as a legal adult
fact_checks.by: WEWS News 5 Cleveland (Morgan Trau), republished by Ohio Capital Journal

fact_checks.claim: Husted took over $116,000 from Epstein associates and voted to block release of the Epstein files (same claims, earlier Brown ad)
fact_checks.rating: No rating (FactCheck.org does not rate). The $116,892 all came from one person, Les Wexner, 2001-2025, and includes $36,992 given to DeWine's campaign or transition fund. A 2019 FBI email listed Wexner as a 'secondary' co-conspirator with 'limited evidence'; he has never been charged. Husted voted Sept. 10, 2025 to block a Democratic amendment to release the files but supported the standalone bill by unanimous consent on Nov. 19, 2025 ('The senator essentially did both'). FactCheck.org did not assess '10 times more'.

fact_checks.claim: Husted's donations from Les Wexner and his Epstein-files vote (same claims, earlier Brown ad)
fact_checks.rating: No Truth-O-Meter rating: 'The Brown ad is correct that Husted received donations from Wexner, but it is missing context'. Husted voted to table the amendment to force release of the files about two months after a $3,500 Wexner donation (his campaign said the vote was about protecting military benefits); the Epstein Files Transparency Act later passed by unanimous consent with no roll call; Husted's campaign gave $34,300 to an anti-trafficking charity.

ads.notes: Selected as the Brown campaign's most recent TV ad found. Opening line as quoted by Metro Weekly (Oct 10, https://www.metroweekly.com/2026/10/sherrod-brown-anti-trans-ad-husted-epstein/), which quotes the remaining lines in the same order with minor punctuation differences; the rest is as printed by Erin in the Morning. Neither source prints the disclaimer, and neither says the quotes are the full script. AdImpact's transcript is labeled AI-generated, so it was not used. The FactCheck.org and PolitiFact checks covered the same donation and vote claims in Brown's May 'Epstein Files' ad (AdImpact first-air 05/01/26). The Ad Wars Dispatch Substack (Oct 11) named this its top ad of the week (an editorial pick, no spend figure). Earlier Brown ad with an official release, full script and YouTube upload: the Sept 29 ':60' spot built on Husted's remarks about people in poverty (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wW4pe2UM3c0; https://www.sherrodbrown.com/2026/09/29/jon-husted-stars-in-new-ad-as-ohioans-react-to-his-own-unedited-insulting-words-talking-down-to-working-ohioans/).

Those lines and findings are known only from the Acton campaign's Oct 8 repost (https://actonforgovernor.com/cleveland-com-vivek-ramaswamy-ad-contains-3-lies-about-his-pharmaceutical-record/). fact_checks.by: TiffinOhio.net (Bonnie Lucas), checking what it called V-PAC's newest TV ad as of Aug 8

fact_checks.claim: Related claim in another pro-Ramaswamy ad ('You know Amy Acton as the COVID lockdown doctor'): Acton is responsible for the COVID lockdowns
fact_checks.rating: No verdict. News 5 reported Acton was DeWine's primary adviser and signed the orders, while DeWine says 'The buck stops with the governor.'

ads.notes: First aired by mid-June 2026 (exact date not reported). Kept under the spec's rule (a): it is the V-PAC ad with the most reported spending (over $8.1M in June). V-PAC's later spots, per TiffinOhio (Aug 8) and News 5 (Aug 31): a July spot on medical-board and police-report material; an early-August spot on a missed CDC training and a TV-remote joke; and a late-August spot with the line 'Drinking, drugs, disaster, disqualified'. On that last one, News 5 found the 2019 Bexley police report describes a verbal dispute with 'no evidence of any physical violence' and does not say Acton was intoxicated (https://www.news5cleveland.com/news/politics/ohio-politics/dr-amy-acton-responds-to-attack-ads-about-alcohol-covid-death). No titles, full scripts or YouTube links were found for any V-PAC ad.

races.notes: NYT (Oct 5, via Boston Globe): 'Ramaswamy backers are outspending the Acton camp on advertising by a more than 3-1 margin' (no dollar figures). Billionaires had given V-PAC a combined $37M, more than 88% of its funding, by mid-2026 (OCJ). OCJ (Jul 22) reported Acton had no super PAC backing her at the time; the DGA-backed Ohioans for Lower Costs released its first ads Aug 19 (TV time booked from Sept 8, per WVXU). Campaign figures come from Ohio Secretary of State filings, not the FEC.
